input.rationale: Cheap source-flagged compaction question worth a focused probe: LeaderState stores accepted indexes in a vector indexed by pid-1 sized to the largest pid, so a configuration with non-contiguous pids leaves placeholder zeros that get_min_all_accepted_idx includes; SequencePaxos::trim then compares the requested index against that minimum. A sparse three-node run is requested to see whether automatic trim is blocked even when every configured node has accepted the entry.

investigations.question: Does the leader's automatic trim compute the minimum accepted index over configured nodes, or do placeholder slots for absent pids force the minimum to 0 in sparse configurations?
investigations.hypothesis: LeaderState::with allocates accepted_indexes with max_pid entries initialized to 0 and indexes them by pid-1. For a configuration such as {1,2,5}, entries for pids 3 and 4 are never updated, so get_min_all_accepted_idx returns 0 even after all three configured nodes accept index 3. SequencePaxos::trim then rejects trim(Some(2)) with NotAllDecided(0) and trim(None) passes 0 to try_trim, compacting nothing, so automatic compaction never progresses.
investigations.discriminator: A three-node {1,2,5} run with three decided entries: the leader's trim(Some(2)) outcome and reported minimum, and the compacted index after trim(None), compared with the minimum accepted index over the three configured nodes.

interpretations.rationale: Source shows the mechanism but not the executed outcome. The leader's accepted_indexes vector is sized by the largest pid and initialized to zero; entries for pids absent from the configuration are never set because accepted indexes only arrive from that node's own Accepted messages. get_min_all_accepted_idx returns the minimum over the whole vector, so absent-pid placeholders pin it to 0. SequencePaxos::trim uses that minimum both as the default trim index and as the bound for an explicit trim index, so for a sparse configuration the leader would report NotAllDecided(0) and never compact, even though every configured node has accepted the entries. Because trim only affects local storage and the forwarded compaction message, this is a compaction/progress defect rather than a safety one. The probe measures the actual trim outcome and the configured nodes' accepted indexes to decide whether the mechanism is reached with real instances.
counterevidence: If the implementation sized or interpreted the accepted-index vector only over configured pids, the minimum would be the true minimum and automatic trim would work; the probe distinguishes this.
The defect would not affect decision safety or agreement; it only leaves storage uncompacted.
A user can always pass an explicit trim index, but the same minimum check bounds it, so an explicit index above 0 is also rejected under the same mechanism.
limitations: No execution receipt yet.
The probe uses majority quorum, unit batch size, memory storage and no snapshots.
Only one sparse layout ({1,2,5}) is exercised; the claim would generalize to any configuration with absent pids below the maximum, which the source argument covers.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?
investigations.hypothesis: The core returns one Trimmed/Snapshotted element in place of the whole trimmed prefix, so the vector is shorter than decided-from. push_to_sub increments next_idx once per element and push_to_all_subs assumes entries[i] is the entry at min_next+i, so after a catch-up that crosses a compaction boundary the cursor lands short of decided and later pushes re-deliver the entries after the compacted index, violating the documented in-order decided stream that applications use to apply entries once.
investigations.discriminator: The actual element count and kinds of read_decided_suffix(from) for from below versus at the compacted index on a real trimmed log, and the first later push computed from the resulting cursor.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run in which entry 5 is decided with four accepting nodes but the Decide reaches only one follower, those nodes elect a new leader whose prepare quorum excludes that follower, and the follower's late promise triggers AcceptSync: the observed decided index and the Decided/Undecided status of the same index before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

gaps.question: Was an AcceptSync carrying node 2's decided index 4 generated for node 5 and applied by node 5, and if not, which guard or routing step prevented it?
Were a Promise from node 5, an AcceptSync to node 5, and an Accepted reply from node 5 actually produced and routed after node 5's late Prepare?

After a late Prepare is delivered with true extraction and the late Promise is delivered only to the leader, does the leader emit an AcceptSync to that follower carrying its lower decided index, and does the follower apply it?

materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.

result.summary: Opened a focused compaction/progress investigation with a three-node {1,2,5} experiment: LeaderState keeps accepted indexes in a pid-indexed vector sized to the largest pid, so absent pids 3 and 4 stay at 0 and get_min_all_accepted_idx returns 0; trim(Some(2)) should be rejected as NotAllDecided(0) and trim(None) should compact nothing even though all configured nodes accepted index 3. investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?
investigations.hypothesis: The core returns one Trimmed/Snapshotted element in place of the whole trimmed prefix, so the vector is shorter than decided-from. push_to_sub increments next_idx once per element and push_to_all_subs assumes entries[i] is the entry at min_next+i, so after a catch-up that crosses a compaction boundary the cursor lands short of decided and later pushes re-deliver the entries after the compacted index, violating the documented in-order decided stream that applications use to apply entries once.
investigations.discriminator: The actual element count and kinds of read_decided_suffix(from) for from below versus at the compacted index on a real trimmed log, and the first later push computed from the resulting cursor.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run in which entry 5 is decided with four accepting nodes but the Decide reaches only one follower, those nodes elect a new leader whose prepare quorum excludes that follower, and the follower's late promise triggers AcceptSync: the observed decided index and the Decided/Undecided status of the same index before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

The probe records read_decided_suffix(1) and (4) shapes and replays the actor's cursor arithmetic from source over those real outputs.

basis.prefix: Build both nodes from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]} and default ServerConfig with pid 1/2 and MemoryStorage. comparisons.description: Requesting from index 1 below compacted 4 returns the compacted marker plus the two remaining entries, so len is 3 while decided_minus_from is 5.
Requesting from the compacted boundary itself returns one element per remaining index (len 2).
The per-element cursor after catch-up is short of decided, so the next push re-delivers entries 5 and 6.

interpretations.rationale: The source establishes the mechanism: a pending append_notify stores only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot), and drain_notifiers resolves Ok whenever decided_idx >= assigned_idx before it checks whether that ballot has been superseded; nothing in the Ok path reads the entry at assigned_idx. The runtime's own tests establish both premises the false Ok would need: Ok(idx) is expected to mean the caller's value is decided at idx, and an entry accepted only on the old leader can be replaced at the same index by a different decided value while the origin learns of the new ballot. What is not yet established is the decisive schedule: the origin's actor drains on each tick (10 ms by default) and when commands arrive, so a drain while decided_idx < assigned_idx and the promise ballot has already changed yields Superseded and avoids the false Ok. A false Ok requires the decided advance to assigned_idx and the ballot change to be visible in the same drain pass, or the decided advance to arrive with the new ballot before any intervening tick. The runtime crate is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos test target, so the fixed assurance_generated harness cannot execute this path; the open question is therefore the actor-level interleaving and log-content identity, not the core Paxos decision rule.
counterevidence: The Superseded doc explicitly calls itself a heuristic and notes the entry can still be decided under the new ballot at log_entry_idx; when the caller's entry survives reconciliation, returning Ok once decided_idx reaches idx is correct and must not be suppressed.

The false-Ok case requires the origin's own minority-accepted entry to be replaced at that index; if the new leader adopts the value, the decided entry at idx is still the caller's entry and Ok is accurate.
limitations: omnipaxos_runtime is not listed in omnipaxos/Cargo.toml dev-dependencies, so tests/assurance_generated.rs in the omnipaxos crate cannot construct the actor or call append_notify.
No execution receipt exists for this question; the account rests on source reading and the runtime's saved test expectations, which describe intent but do not establish a schedule.

The hash-free timing of tokio channel delivery and the actor's select_biased loop is unmeasured here; the 10 ms tick and 1 ms egress defaults in RuntimeConfig are configuration, not observed interleaving.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading gives a concrete mechanism. In InternalStorage::read, when from is below the compacted index the result is one create_compacted_entry element followed by one element per entry from compacted_idx to the requested end, so for from < compacted_idx the vector has fewer elements than decided_idx - from; the Trimmed(t)/Snapshotted variant is a marker for the whole trimmed prefix, not one index. The runtime stores only next_idx per subscriber, increments it once per element pushed (push_to_sub and push_to_all_subs), and push_to_all_subs computes start = sub.next_idx - min_next assuming one element per index. A subscription or catch-up at from < compacted therefore ends with next_idx = from + 1 + (decided - compacted), short of decided, and the next push re-reads from that cursor and re-sends entries after the compacted index. subscribe_decided accepts any from and documents a single in-order stream; nothing rejects or compensates for a compacted starting index. The retained execution is needed to pin the core's returned shape (element count and kinds) and the resulting replay; the claim remains unresolved until that receipt is associated.
counterevidence: If the caller only ever subscribes at or above the compacted index, read_decided_suffix returns exactly one element per index and the cursor arithmetic is aligned; the defect is limited to a starting or lagging cursor below compaction.
A Trimmed/Snapshotted marker is a documented LogEntry variant, so delivering it is not itself wrong; the defect is the cursor advance that treats the marker as one index.

The probe reproduces the actor's cursor arithmetic over real core outputs; that reproduction is a reconstruction of source logic, not an execution of the runtime crate.

interpretations.rationale: The pending completion path can report a false success, under a schedule the actor does not exclude. A pending append_notify keeps only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot). drain_notifiers evaluates, in order, Ok when assigned_idx <= decided, then Superseded when the assignment ballot is below the current promise ballot, then Timeout; the Ok arm reads no log entry and never checks that the value at assigned_idx is the caller's entry. The origin can hold an assignment made when it was leader or when a leader accepted its proposal, lose leadership to a higher ballot, and then have its own decided index advance past assigned_idx with a different value at that index: the runtime's own Superseded regression test constructs exactly that replacement (the old leader accepts locally with its outgoing cut, a new leader appends a fresh entry that decides at the same index, and the origin learns of the new ballot). Whether the pending resolves Ok or Superseded then depends only on whether a drain runs after the promise advanced but before decided reached assigned_idx. drain_notifiers runs only in the actor's tick branch; handling an incoming message never drains. Nothing orders a tick between the ballot change and the decided advance, so when the origin processes the higher-ballot Prepare and then the message that carries decided >= assigned_idx within one tick interval, the Ok arm wins and the caller is told its entry is decided at an index that holds a different entry. With a legal user-set tick_period that exceeds the leadership-turnover interval, that ordering is deterministic; with a short period it is a race. The gap on the reachable schedule is therefore answered on source grounds: no mechanism prevents it, and a legal configuration makes it the expected ordering.

3f84facd1a81451882518e32ee8be535-gap-0.explanation: Reachable. drain_notifiers is invoked only from the tick branch (actor.rs tick handling), while handle_incoming_tracked processes messages without draining; the actor polls the tick first each iteration but the tick fires at most once per configured period. The ballot change (Prepare/AcceptSync from the new leader) and the decided advance (AcceptDecide/Decide from that leader) are separate messages that can both be processed inside one period. If the period exceeds the turnover interval, the pending sees decided >= assigned_idx and a stale assignment ballot at the same drain, and the Ok arm precedes the Superseded arm. Since tick_period is user-set and only advised to match the ServerConfig tick budget, this ordering is legal and deterministic in that configuration.

- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.
